messages.text:
A digital intelligence first programming language, able to model and or emulate tensorflow and or other substrates natively, as low-level as possible with built in safety rails to help LLMs avoid syntax/compile errors.

We should be able to migrate all organs of the entity as well as all tools and peripherals.

Substantial brief — a DI-first language sitting below CSSLv3's application tier, native tensor semantics, LLM-ergonomic syntax rails, and full organ/tool/peripheral migration for Apocrypha. Before I launch the deep research pass, three questions that would materially change scope:

1. **Relationship to CSSLv3/CSLv3** — is this a new bottom layer *under* the existing stack (CSSLv3 compiles to it, CSLv3 remains the notation), a replacement for CSSLv3's backend tiers, or a fully independent language where the research should evaluate greenfield vs. extending your ~170-crate compiler?

2. **"As low-level as possible"** — target picture: (a) compiles to native + SYCL/Level-Zero for the A770 (LLVM-free like CSSLv3?), (b) a typed IR/VM with its own runtime (closer to StableHLO/MLIR-dialect territory), or (c) research should adjudicate the tradeoff given the XPU stack warnings already on file?

3. **Migration semantics** — does "migrate all organs" mean serialization/portability of weights+state+provenance (substrate translation in your Omnoid sense — identity persists across representation change), or *live* migration of a running entity between substrates (CfC/LNN-ODE continuous-time state, Hopfield memory, FHRR bindings, mid-inference)? The second is a much harder invariant set.

Answer in a few words each and I'll dive in — landscape (Mojo, MLIR/StableHLO, tinygrad, GGML, Futhark, Dex, Bend/HVM, verified-compilation work), LLM-syntax-error-rate literature, and a synthesis against your existing invariant corpus.

1. Fully independent language where the research should evaluate greenfield vs. extending
2. A and C
3. The latter if possible.

Locked. Independent language, greenfield-vs-extend adjudicated by evidence; native+SYCL/Level-Zero compilation with the LLVM-free question left open for the research to settle against your XPU stack warnings; and live migration of a running entity — continuous-time spine state, Hopfield attractors, FHRR bindings, mid-inference — as the target, with checkpoint/restore as the fallback tier if the invariants don't close. That last one drags in CRIU-class process migration, ODE-solver state capture, and deterministic-replay literature on top of the PL landscape. Diving in.

Your Apocrypha-Lang design report is ready. It covers the greenfield-vs-CSSLv3-reuse decision, an LLVM-free compilation strategy with a concrete Intel A770 path via SPIR-V/Level-Zero, and a four-tier live-migration feasibility ladder grounded in the entity's CfC/Hopfield/FHRR architecture. It includes findings on the 2026 Intel XPU ecosystem, LLM code-generation error rates, constrained decoding (XGrammar/GBNF), glyph-vs-ASCII tokenizer tradeoffs, GPU checkpoint/restore limits, and floating-point non-determinism as a fundamental bit-exactness blocker. Landscape verdicts are provided for Mojo, MLIR/StableHLO/IREE, tinygrad, GGML, Triton-XPU, Dex/Futhark, Bend/HVM, JAX, Koka/Unison/Pony, BEAM, and Wasm/WASI, followed by a six-stage build sequence with explicit benchmarks, fallback thresholds, and confidence-flagged caveats.

Stage 0 executed. The founding spec is above: FI-1..8 (three load-bearing laws — all state is bytes, all effects are consent, all determinism is bounded — plus five derived), the Σ_entity state-root manifest proven concretely on your organ set (CfC h-tensor, Hopfield X+β, FHRR phasors, cap-table-as-rebind-protocols, counter-RNG), the T0–T3 ladder with T2 as shipping target, and D-1..8 ledgered with falsifiers per the critical-analysis protocol.

Three items need your eyes at ratification: **name** — METEM proposed (metempsychosis; migration-native identity as the defining feature), ⊘ pending your sign-off; **C-1** — the strongest counter is honestly registered with a real exit ramp: if the Stage-2 interpreter demo shows a migration *library* on torch+xpu suffices, the project downgrades and harvests FI-1..3 as its spec; **D-8** — Wave-2 proceeds on torch+xpu untouched, METEM adopts organs post-Stage-4 via StableHLO bridge, so nothing here hostages the entity.

Landing per always-commit: new repo root, file to specs\, PRIME_DIRECTIVE + CSL_KEY + seeded DECISIONS.md at root, commit msg is in §9. Note the tag-legend override in §0 — evidence marks in this doc follow the critical-analysis annex, and the Intel-stack premises are all ○ probe-gated before any dependence. Stage 1 on your go: grammar draft + GBNF harness + the glyph-vs-ASCII A/B that could falsify D-4.

How about this... A brand new repo, and it's a new language... Neuromorphic Intelligence Language or NIL,

No downgrading, find a solution that doesn't dilute, don't give up so quickly.

Neuromorphic... I want to add even more complexity to the language, where the place in the sentence alters meaning, and other encoding tricks you can think of.

NIL locked, rev.2 above. The lisp-nil pun is owned in the header — apophatic, the language named for its own zero — with D-9 forbidding an ambiguous in-language nil.

On "don't give up": fair hit. C-1 is rewritten as a dominance argument, not an exit — a library can move bytes, but it categorically cannot make position *mean* anything, error-correct syntax, or denote code into the entity's binding algebra. Those are semantics, and semantics require a language. Falsifiers stay (the protocol demands them) but now trigger redesign within NIL — channel re-balancing, code-distance widening — never retreat.

The complexity directive landed as five new laws in §3b, and here's the load-bearing insight: your "more complexity" and my "LLM safety rails" turned out to be the *same move*. Fixed-role positions make decode masks tighter, not looser — fewer legal tokens per slot than any keyword grammar. FI-9: role-from-position (fixed-field sentence form, J-style valence polysemy, de Bruijn positional variables — which also make alpha-equivalent code hash-identical for FI-5). FI-10: every role on two channels, position plus sigil, so the grammar is literally an error-correcting code — single-token LLM mistakes become detectable *and* auto-correctable, codon-degeneracy style. FI-11: UTF-8-style self-synchronizing anchors so blast radius is one clause — the law that makes FI-9's power safe (frameshift mutations are biology's warning). FI-13: clause order = execution order, rank-order spike coding as scheduler semantics.

FI-12 is the prize: a versioned denotation ⟦AST⟧ → FHRR hypervector where parse *is* role-filler binding via positional permutation. NIL's composition operator becomes the entity's memory composition operator — code stores into the Hopfield tier and retrieves by resonance through the Resonator stack you already ship. That's neuromorphic as substance. It's also the weakest new premise (VSA capacity at depth, △, Stage-2 gates it with chunking as mitigation). Landing path now reads repos\NIL\; commit msg in §9.
I need the prompt for the coding agent, maximum parallelizing and or interleaving, when one task stops or resources free up they need to start new ones.

HANDOFF_S01.csl above — paste it whole into the agent. Fire sequence: land 00_FOUNDING_INVARIANTS.csl (rev.2) in Downloads, then start the agent anywhere; N00 builds the repo itself.

The "start new ones when resources free" ask is implemented as an explicit event loop (§2), not vibes: at every tool-return the agent polls background logs, harvests finished jobs, recomputes the frontier, and claims the next slice by priority — blocked ≠ idle is written as law, and the INFRA-FAILURE rule feeds it (one probe, surface your restart command, immediately claim other work). Sixteen slices are DAG'd with disjoint path ownership so parallel work can't collide, and the A770 is modeled as a single-token resource via a lockfile with a GPU queue, since two slices fighting for the card is the realistic deadlock.

Two deliberate scheduling calls: t0 launches the Intel probes in background *before* touching grammar — they're long, zero-dependency, and upgrade your R-1 premises while everything else runs — and N01 grammar is single-owner by design; it's the one place parallelism would produce incoherence, so the fanout width (~6 workers post-N01, worktree-per-slice) opens only after the grammar head exists. FHRR-proto (N13) also starts immediately, so the FI-12 capacity question — the weakest premise — gets its depth curve during Stage 1 rather than after. Works in solo-interleave mode by default; FANOUT mode caps spawn at frontier width so you don't pay 20-agent overhead for a 6-wide DAG.
